slides.headline: Reading the Bible out loud and then closing it is not the same as understanding it.
The gap between those two things is usually four questions.
body: Dr Titi Sodipo took them from the Discovery Bible Study approach.

slides.headline: What do you like in this passage?
body: WHY IT WORKS: it gives everyone permission to answer, including the youngest person in the room.

slides.headline: What is difficult, or challenging?
body: WHY IT WORKS: it makes honesty normal. A household where nobody admits confusion is not a safe place to grow.

slides.headline: What do we learn about God here?
body: WHY IT WORKS: it moves the passage off you and onto Him. Most bad theology begins with reading yourself as the main character.

slides.headline: What do we learn about people, or about yourself?
body: WHY IT WORKS: it turns the passage into a mirror. The first three questions can stay comfortable. This one cannot.

slides.eyebrow: THE BEREANS GOT NAMED FOR EXACTLY THIS

scripture.text: The people of Berea were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica, and they listened eagerly to Paul's message. They searched the Scriptures day after day to see if Paul and Silas were teaching the truth.

slides.kicker: Scripture calls that open-minded. Not disloyal.

slides.headline: Come ready to obey, not only to discuss.
body: John 15:10. When you obey, you remain in His love.
Understanding you never act on is just information.

slides.headline: Read six verses tonight and ask the four questions.
You do not need to be the expert in the room.
body: You need to be the one who asks the questions.
